record.paper_title: The formation and evolution of early-type galaxies : solid results and open questions
record.context_brief: Formation channels for massive early-type galaxies
record.original_question: How did massive early-type galaxies form and evolve, given that early-type galaxies are elliptical and lenticular galaxies and that observations indicate massive systems formed at redshift z > 2 on very short timescales? A self-contained answer should identify which physical channels among starbursts, mergers, secular evolution, and smooth gas accretion can build massive spheroids at high redshift, and should explain how candidate precursor populations selected at z > 2 relate to the later early-type galaxy population.

evidence.quote: HOW DID MASSIVE EARLY-TYPE GALAXIES FORM ?

The properties of ETGs illustrated in previous sections indicate that the massive systems formed at z > 2 with very short timescales. Examples of precursor candidates have been found amongst starburst galaxies selected at z > 2 with a variety of techniques: sBzK

The emerging scenario indicates that, in addition to merging, also secular evolution and smooth accretion of gas play a role in building up disks and massive spheroids at high redshifts, even without major mergers

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Early-type galaxies (ETGs) are defined as elliptical and lenticular galaxies, characterized by spheroidal morphologies, predominantly old stellar populations, low specific star-formation rates, and tight scaling relations (e.g., the fundamental plane, color–magnitude, and mass–size relations). Observations of massive ETGs (stellar mass M_* ≳ 10^{11} M_sun) show that the bulk of their stars formed at redshift z > 2 on short timescales (≲ 1 Gyr), as inferred from α-element enhancement, evolved stellar populations, and the existence of massive, passive, compact galaxies already in place at z ≈ 2.

Determine, in a quantitatively consistent way, the physical formation and evolution channels of massive early-type galaxies. Specifically:

(a) Identify which combination of the following channels is responsible for assembling the stellar mass of massive spheroids by z ≈ 2 and for their subsequent evolution to z = 0: (i) intense, short-lived starbursts at high redshift; (ii) major and minor mergers (dissipative ''wet'' and dissipationless ''dry''); (iii) secular evolution of disks; (iv) smooth cold-gas accretion along cosmological filaments.

(b) Establish the quantitative relationship between candidate high-redshift precursor populations selected at z > 2 (for instance star-forming BzK-selected galaxies (sBzK), submillimeter galaxies, distant red galaxies, Lyman-break galaxies, and massive compact quiescent galaxies) and the population of present-day massive early-type galaxies, including the mapping between progenitors and descendants in stellar mass, number density, size, and clustering.

Provide a self-consistent scenario, compatible with current cosmological structure formation, that specifies the relative contributions (mass fractions and number-density evolution) of channels (i)–(iv) and identifies which observed z > 2 populations evolve into the local massive ETG population.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of how massive early-type galaxies form and evolve remains an active and open research area in extragalactic astrophysics. While significant progress has been made (two-phase formation scenarios, recognition of dry minor mergers driving size growth from z~2 to z=0, role of cold accretion and secular processes, identification of compact ''red nugget'' progenitors), no consensus quantitative model uniquely identifies precursor populations or the relative weights of starbursts, mergers, secular evolution, and smooth accretion. Recent reviews and JWST-era observations continue to refine but not close the question.

status_evidence.title: The formation of early-type galaxies: a review
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews progress on ETG formation noting two-phase formation and ongoing debate over the relative roles of mergers vs in-situ star formation.
status_evidence.claim: ETG formation channels remain debated, with multiple processes contributing.

status_evidence.title: Massive compact quiescent galaxies at z~2
status_evidence.snippet: Compact massive quiescent galaxies at z~2 indicate rapid early formation but their evolution into local ETGs is not fully understood.
status_evidence.claim: Mapping z>2 precursors to local ETGs is still unresolved.
